claim: A localhost-only app cannot receive Google Calendar push or MS Graph change-notifications; both require a public HTTPS endpoint with a valid CA cert. Polling (Google syncToken / Graph delta) is the supported path.
Microsoft has NO native CalDAV endpoint (only Graph/EWS/EAS); Google supports CalDAV v2 but its REST API is preferred. A CalDAV-only design cannot cover Outlook. → two native REST clients required.

OAuth2 Auth-Code+PKCE + Google Calendar v3 + Graph REST is feasible with Python stdlib only (urllib/http.server/ssl/secrets/hashlib + ctypes-DPAPI). PKCE removes the need for a confidential client secret for both providers.

CRACK in stdlib-only: local id_token JWT signature verification needs RSA verify, which is NOT in stdlib hashlib. Avoidable by not verifying id_token locally (trust the TLS-protected token response) or by using a library.

Judge ruling (HIGH confidence): declare a [calendar] optional extra (msal+google-auth) rather than hand-roll OAuth; the [terminal]=pywinpty exception is the exact precedent (stdlib-only is a distribution rule with a scoped-extra escape hatch); hand-rolled token lifecycle is a silent-failure liability for a one-maintainer app.

Two-way correctness model: mapping table keyed by iCalUID + last-synced baseline three-way merge (Unison/vdirsyncer), echo-suppression via etag+self-marker, tombstones for deletes, recurring master+exception. vdirsyncer is the canonical open-source algorithm.

The markdown-line data model is lossy by construction for real calendar events (cannot represent RRULE/EXDATE/VTIMEZONE/attendees); round-tripping arbitrary events two-way through markdown-as-source-of-truth manufactures recurring-event corruption + data loss. → phase: pull+display, then one-way push of Anchor-authored deadlines, defer full two-way.

Google 'Testing' publishing mode revokes refresh tokens for the sensitive calendar scope every 7 days; move the OAuth app to 'Production' (may remain unverified for personal single-user use; 100-user cap + consent warning are non-issues). Calendar is a SENSITIVE (not restricted) scope.

Microsoft refresh tokens ROTATE — the new RT must be persisted on every refresh. MSA vs work/school account type changes consent/token semantics and the /common vs /consumers authority; Conditional Access can force interactive re-auth.

The anchor NSSM service runs as .\john (SERVICE_START_NAME : .\john), NOT LocalSystem. → DPAPI user-scope is the correct token-encryption primitive and the one-time browser consent runs in John's interactive session. Corrects a stale 'LocalSystem' note in the runtime-facts memory.

DPAPI via ctypes CryptProtectData works pure-stdlib (no pywin32); blobs are user+machine bound → a machine migration / profile-SID change makes stored tokens permanently undecryptable (silent re-auth). Anchor's DPAPI-wrapped store is strictly better than the surrounding plaintext claude/gemini OAuth creds on this box.

Most dangerous risk = a two-way sync bug silently deleting/duplicating REAL events (irreversible, blast radius outside Anchor). Cheapest fix (one config field): Anchor reads all calendars but only ever WRITES to a dedicated 'Anchor' calendar it owns per provider — never holds a delete/update handle on a human-created event.

Codebase fit: distro.py's import scan blocks any calendar SDK except a declared scoped exception; new calendar_auth.py/calendar_sync.py are auto-first-party; tokens/state belong under .anchor/calendar/ (auto-excluded from distro); polling must run on a background daemon thread (existing _trigger_session_summary pattern); render reads cache only; fully-stubbed healthcheck (never live Google/MS) per the v2-v7 standard.

Honesty: all findings are doc-corroborated, NOT code-OBSERVED — no live OAuth dance or API call executed. Riskiest unspiked claim: 'Production-but-unverified holds a durable refresh token for the sensitive calendar scope' — verify with a real >7-day token-survival spike before committing Phase A.
